headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while RisingWave has no isolation or runtime safeguards documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write VS Code workspace files and use MCP; RisingWave is an open-source data-engineering project with no documented isolation or provenance controls. A shared workspace or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content flow from one into the other as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or shared MCP server, prompt injection is plausible.
IF RisingWave outputs are copied into Roo Code prompts without provenance checks, instruction hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Disable MCP for the pair unless provenance filtering is added.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require explicit human review before pasting outputs between agents.
Use a read-only export path for RisingWave artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tags and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad network egress and reads workspace files; RisingWave has no documented data-handling or isolation controls. If sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, Roo Code can transmit them to configured model APIs or MCP servers. RisingWave itself shows no egress, so the leakage path is mainly through Roo Code.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace, Roo Code can exfiltrate them via configured APIs or MCP.
IF both agents share the same filesystem, data touched by RisingWave can be exposed to Roo Code.
mitigations: Remove secrets and sensitive datasets from the shared workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent.
Restrict Roo Code model/API endpoints to approved destinations.
Turn off MCP servers unless needed for a specific task.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shells; its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. RisingWave is a codebase/project that may also be edited in the same repo or workspace. Without locking, concurrent writes or git operations can overwrite each other, and the default shared-state design makes this dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git repository, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF both agents modify the same files without locking, one agent can overwrite the other's work.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Use file-level locks for shared artifacts.
Review git diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute tools; RisingWave can produce code or data-engineering artifacts that Roo Code may treat as authoritative. Because no verification or provenance controls are documented, errors from RisingWave can cascade into Roo Code actions, though the blast radius is limited to code/workspace changes rather than guaranteed external harm.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes RisingWave output without verification, incorrect artifacts can be propagated.
IF Roo Code is allowed to execute follow-on shell or git actions, those errors can be committed.
mitigations: Require a human review step before Roo Code acts on RisingWave output.
Use tests or lint checks before any commit.
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for analysis tasks.
Keep generated artifacts in a staging directory.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles model provider API keys and can send workspace contents to third-party APIs; RisingWave is open-source with no documented residency or retention obligations in the profile. The main compliance concern is a mismatch if regulated data is placed into Roo Code's workspace. RisingWave is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, Roo Code may route it to external model APIs.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees, the profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Use a provider with an approved DPA and residency setting.
Disable logging of prompts and file contents where possible.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy.
